headline: Computational frameworks link transcriptomic and metabolomic data to disease signatures
label: Computational Multiomics Frameworks
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply integrative omics, benchmarking, and inference frameworks to pathway, metabolite, and single-cell analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational integration of multi-omic and public cohort data to derive interpretable molecular signatures or inference frameworks. Several items bridge transcriptomic and metabolic readouts: CHIMERA maps scRNA-seq to single-cell metabolite abundances using spatially paired Visium data, and MetaboGraph performs direction-aware pathway inference on metabolomics and lipidomics. Others derive gene signatures from public bulk and single-cell cohorts, including the ER stress and lactylation studies, while PRISM-MM and SwitchClass address state-resolved feature decomposition in drug response and intermediate molecular states. The SPRAS preprint provides the most explicit methodological comparison, a registered-report benchmark of 14 pathway reconstruction algorithms across 822 datasets. What is new is mainly the application of these pipelines to specific conditions and the proposed mapping from transcriptome to metabolome.
